messages:
jen (eng-infra): Heads up — we're seeing a weird migration loop in ap-southeast1 where tiny GPU pods get bound, quickly evicted, then immediately rescheduled to different nodes.
akshay (scheduler): I noticed. Scheduler logs show a cascade of "node matches but taint not tolerated" errors followed by preemptive backfills. Looks like fractional gang placement + node-level taints are fighting.
linda (oncall): Any customer-facing impact yet? latency/cold starts?
jen (eng-infra): A couple of internal test jobs hit OOM/restarts from eviction churn. External SLAs look fine but tokenized workloads see higher p99 latency. Cost spike for the region (extra preemptions + reschedules).
sre-bot: alert: gpu-pending-count-ap-southeast1 > 40 for 5m :warning:
scheduler-bot: auto-scale event: expanded warm-pool ap-southeast1 by 2 nodes at 1767895420
akshay (scheduler): Root cause trace: warm-pool allocation picks nodes with taints: gpu:reserved=low-tier:NoSchedule. New tiny-gang pods require tolerant: gpu:reserved=low-tier but our admission path strips tolerations for dedicated pools because of an optimization bug.
maria (eng-platform): That admission optimization was the patch from last week (speed up binding). Could it be dropping tolerations on small pods when warmpool=true?
jen (eng-infra): Yep. Quick reproduction:

```
# failing pod repro
kubectl -n ml get pod tiny-gang-xx -o yaml
# spec shows tolerations missing, nodeSelector matches, but node has taint gpu:reserved=low-tier:NoSchedule
```

And scheduler log excerpt:
```
I0318 12:45:21.123 scheduler.go:482] admit: pod tiny-gang-xx matched node n-gpu-23, but taint gpu:reserved=low-tier:NoSchedule not tolerated
I0318 12:45:21.124 scheduler.go:488] preempting small idle pods to fit gang -> causes reschedule -> cycle
```
linda (oncall): Ok, mitigation plan? We should avoid thrash and reduce cost while we patch.
akshay (scheduler): Short-term: revert the admission optimization that drops tolerations (deploy revert to canary in ap-southeast1). Also add a scheduler rule to prefer nodes without gpu:reserved taint for fractional gangs to avoid preemption loops.
maria (eng-platform): Could also add a temporary admission webhook override to re-inject tolerations for tiny-gang pods in that namespace.
jen (eng-infra): Revert PR queued. I'll roll a canary revert to 2 nodes in ap-southeast1 now. Also propose increasing preemption_grace (preempt window) from 5s to 30s to reduce rapid churn.
linda (oncall): Do the revert and the grace change as a single deploy? prefer separate so we can rollback individually.
akshay (scheduler): agree, separate. I'll push a scheduler config tweak to bump preempt window and add a logging gate so we can see if churn drops.
jen (eng-infra): Costs: current estimate shows ~12% increase in reschedule token spend in that AZ last hour. If we delay fix >2h, it'll be another ~$1.2k.
maria (eng-platform): Noted. Can we also run a short job to identify other regions that have the same admission optimization enabled? Might preemptively break elsewhere.
jen (eng-infra): Doing a grep across clusters for webhook version v2.4.1 — returns eu-west1b with the same build. I'll add it to the rollout watchlist.

```
# simple query
kubectl --context=cluster-eu-west1b get mutatingwebhookconfiguration | grep admit-opt
```

akshay (scheduler): Action items:
- jen: revert admission change in ap-southeast1 canary (in progress) (1767895445)
- akshay: sched config bump preempt window to 30s in canary (1767895460)
- maria: scan other regions and post list (1767895475)
- linda: monitor pager for regressions and customer impact (oncall)

linda (oncall): I'll mute noisy alerts for now and keep oncall loop informed. If churn goes down, unmute and mark incident resolved.
jen (eng-infra): Revert deployed to canary (2 nodes) at 1767895455. Watching pod churn.
scheduler-bot: metric: preemptions_ap-southeast1 count=34 -> 7 (5m window)
akshay (scheduler): Early signal looks good. Preemptions dropped to single digits and pending GPU count fell to 12.
maria (eng-platform): eu-west1b also has the webhook; I'll open a PR to schedule a canary revert there tomorrow, unless we ship a proper fix.
jen (eng-infra): Long-term fix: admission should preserve tolerations for pods bound to dedicated/warm pools; also add unit test in the mutating webhook to prevent regressions.

jen (eng-infra): Thanks team. Leaving the canary up for 30m, then promote region-wide if stable. Will post a short postmortem after full rollback/prod fix.

linda (oncall): Good work. :thumbsup:
